items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: The interviewee discusses Honegger only in response to the interviewer's anecdote about playing a Honegger piece; the interviewee does not mention any personal interaction, collaboration, or direct acquaintance with Honegger.

ctx.x: I agree, yeah. We’re all in the same love situation, you know? We like music. We like jazz. I mean jazz has been my first preference. But I like playing symphonic stuff. I played with Leopold Stokowski and that was a lot of fun. In his last three years in this country, and I was fortunate enough to get principal bass in his orchestra and you’d always end up sweating with him you know, even if you were hung over, you’d go into a rehearsal and in about a half hour you’re sweating you know. He really made you play.

Do you think modern classical music is — I’m not sure where “modern” starts but — more difficult to play than the classics, the Romantic period and Baroque music? That’s a wide question but I once had an experience playing a Honegger piece and there was a saxophone part and man I could not keep track of where it was. It was so harmonically dense and of course they had 60 bars of rest before I came in and talk about sweating. Please give me a cue.

Yeah. Well you know you’re getting into a controversial area you know. There was a book called — now I can’t remember, damn — The Agony of Modern Music by Henry Pleasants. And he said the real modern music is jazz, because like from Stravinsky on you know it got so complicated with different time signatures and it’s like a made-up idiom sort of because the complexity of playing contemporary music, it’s like you don’t know what style — I mean you have to learn the style of each individual composer but it’s like —…
